## OSM-derived route data

The full used-node version manifests are listed below.

## Elevation provenance and deterministic metrics

Elevation was researched once per relation through the [Open-Meteo Elevation API](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/elevation-api), whose Copernicus DEM GLO-90 attribution is retained in the source card. Each request sampled cumulative-distance-equal WGS84 points, included first and last, and stayed at or below 100 points; no failed oversized request was retried.

| Relation | Request points | Response points | Provider |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 16162196 | 100 | 100 | Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo |
| 20072118 | 89 | 89 | Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo |
| 20046643 | 85 | 85 | Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo |
| 20739620 | 98 | 98 | Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo |
| 17841828 | 100 | 100 | Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo |

The runtime stores no query URLs or response payloads. Elevation values on the full geometry are linearly interpolated between the sampled points. Ascent/descent sum positive/negative adjacent elevation deltas; highest is the maximum sampled/interpolated elevation. Planar distance uses WGS84 Haversine (Earth radius 6,371,008.8 m), then floors to three decimal kilometres. Duration is deterministic (distanceKm / 4 + ascentM / 600), rounded to two decimals, and the frozen variants are one-day stages.
